content:
In the dissolution of a legal community, Art. 194 CC dictates an equal division of assets regardless of individual economic contributions made during the marriage. The interpretative issue concerns the nature of the legal community as a "community without shares," which prevents applying ordinary co-ownership rules regarding proof of different financial inputs. The Court established that while pre-dissolution contributions are irrelevant, only documented expenses (e.g., mortgage or condominium fees) paid by one spouse after the formal dissolution of the regime are eligible for reimbursement.

A spouse requested compensation for the other's exclusive enjoyment of the marital home post-separation. The legal problem is whether exclusive possession automatically generates a right to indemnity. Applying Art. 1102 CC, the Court ruled that exclusive use is not inherently detrimental. No indemnity is due unless the claimant provides specific evidence of the property's rental value and proves they were actively prevented from using the asset, a burden of proof that was not met in the present case.
